transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-20
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Camila (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Maya (Hypatia VP Eng), Jon (Hypatia Platform), Asha (Hypatia Security)

Summary:
- Hypatia evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted API for dev and a Dedicated/private deployment for production-critical routes.
- Main concerns: multi-region failover, incident tolerance, SLA commitments (latency & availability), data residency and KMS integration.
- Agreed next steps: send security pack, run SE-led benchmark, discuss pricing for a short Dedicated pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Camila: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Camila with Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. We also have Ethan, our solutions engineer, with us. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good, thanks. Maya here. We've been looking at Redwood as a potential inference layer. Wanted to cover reliability and incident tolerance before next steps.
[00:15] Jon: Yeah, specifically multi-region fallbacks, and how dedicated vs hosted would handle a region outage.
[00:22] Camila: Great, that's exactly what we wanted to walk through. Ethan, want to kick off with the runtime and fallback story?
[00:28] Ethan: Sure. So at a high level, Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private options. For reliability we do a couple of things — smart routing by policy, model variants for graceful degradation, and multi-region routing with automatic fallback.
[00:40] Ethan: In hosted mode we have regional endpoints and cross-region failover. In case of regional outage we route to the next healthy region, which may hit a different model variant to keep latency within SLOs. For Dedicated you can provision dedicated pools in multiple regions; we can also do cross-region mirroring for key state if you require that.
[01:01] Jon: When you say model variant, do you mean like a quantized smaller model as a fallback? How transparent is that to the app?
[01:08] Ethan: Exactly. We support configured fallback chains. Primary model can be a high-capacity model, fallback could be a smaller quantized variant. It's transparent at the API layer — you get the same endpoint but the response characteristics will differ. We tag responses with model metadata so you can detect fallbacks in your logs.
[01:25] Asha: From security - how do you handle key management for private deployments? We need to integrate with our customer-managed KMS and also ensure audit logs.
[01:33] Ethan: For Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. Audit logs are available in the console and we can stream them to your syslog/S3. We'll include the SOC 2 / ISO pack and the KMS integration guide in the follow-up.
[01:45] Maya: Our primary SLO is 99.99 availability for the payment auth route, and p95 latency <= 200ms for short prompts. Is that realistic?
[01:53] Ethan: 99.99 is achievable with Dedicated plus cross-region redundancy and proper autoscale policies. For p95 200ms it's highly dependent on sequence length and model size. For short prompts and smaller model variants you can hit that. The key is placement — put the Dedicated pool close to your region and use smart routing for burst spillover.
[02:13] Camila: To add, we often recommend a hybrid: Hosted for developer-facing non-critical routes and Dedicated for high-SLA production traffic. That reduces cost while preserving reliability.
[02:23] Jon: Do you do KV cache replication across regions? We rely heavily on prefix caching and session KV.
[02:29] Ethan: Good question. We do KV cache local to the serving node for latency; for multi-region redundancy we provide configurable cache warmers and prefix caching strategies. Full realtime KV replication across regions adds latency, so we recommend an eventual-consistent warm-up + synchronous fallback to a model variant if cache miss patterns cause latency spikes.
[02:48] Maya: That sounds... reasonable. If there's a region outage, do you route traffic instantly? What's the TTL for failover?
[02:55] Ethan: We detect regional failures via health probes and provider metrics; typical failover is sub-30s for routing at the control plane level, but user-perceived recovery depends on cold-starts for model warming. We have warm start pools and pre-warmed standby replicas for critical routes to keep cold-starts under control.
[03:13] Maya: Any observable tags to know if traffic hit a fallback or different model? We need that for audit and QA.
[03:18] Ethan: Yes, every response includes model_id, model_variant, region, and a fallback_reason tag if a fallback was used. That shows up in the dashboard and can be forwarded to your logging/trace system.
[03:29] Asha: About SLAs — what do your uptime and latency SLAs look like for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:36] Camila: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime commitments (we can share the exact contract language), typically expressed as monthly uptime percentage with credits. For Hosted we provide published SLOs but Dedicated is the one you can commit to in contract. We'll share a sample MSA and SLA appendix.
[03:50] Jon: In an outage, what's the post-incident process? How do we get root cause and timeline?
[03:56] Camila: We provide incident reports for Dedicated customers with timeline, RCA, and any mitigations. For high-tier contracts we can add access to live incident bridge or direct engineering liaison.
[04:06] Maya: We're also concerned about data residency. Some routes must stay in EU. Can routing be tag/route-level so EU traffic never leaves region?
[04:14] Ethan: Yes, routing policies can be route- or token-level. You can pin a route to EU-only Dedicated pools and mark it as non-failover if you need strict residency. Alternatively, you can allow failover to a compliant region if approved.
[04:29] Jon: Great. What about canary rollouts for model versions? We want to avoid regressions when upgrading models.
[04:35] Ethan: We support canary and gradual rollouts with percent-based traffic splits, A/B experiments, automatic rollback on error or quality regressions. We also integrate quality monitoring tied to prompt sets — if you provide a prompt set we can surface regression alerts.
[04:50] Maya: For our pilots we'd like to run a dedicated pilot for the payment auth route and keep dev on hosted. What's the minimum commit for Dedicated?
[04:58] Camila: Minimum committed capacity depends on region/hardware; I'll include typical sizing and pricing. We can do a short pilot (month) with a reduced commit and a plan to scale if benchmarks look good.
[05:08] Asha: Quick security clarifications: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit retention, and encryption at rest.
[05:14] Ethan: All supported. SSO via SAML/SCIM, granular RBAC, configurable audit retention, encryption at rest with customer-managed keys for Private/Dedicated. We'll attach the security checklist.
[05:26] Maya: Can you outline the benchmark plan now? What data do you need?
[05:30] Ethan: We'll need a representative prompt corpus, typical session lengths, QPS profile and peak concurrency, and any strict p95/p99 latency requirements. We'll run two passes: a functional correctness pass across your prompt set, then load tests simulating peak traffic including failover scenarios and multi-region routing.
[05:50] Jon: On failover sim — can you simulate region outage and show response behavior?
[05:54] Ethan: Yes, as part of the benchmark we can simulate a regional outage and measure failover time, cold-starts, and p95/p99 under failover. We can also validate cache warm-up strategies.
[06:06] Maya: About logs — can we stream request/response metadata to our SIEM? We can’t stream PII payloads, but metadata and model tags are fine.
[06:13] Ethan: Absolutely. We can push audit logs and response metadata to your S3 or to a log endpoint; payload filtering rules are configurable.
[06:20] Camila: Let me say something about cost tradeoffs: multi-region Dedicated obviously increases compute cost but reduces failover time and gives you predictable performance. The hybrid approach often saves money while meeting SLAs for critical routes.
[06:33] Maya: Do you have any examples or customers in fintech with similar constraints?
[06:37] Camila: Yes, we've worked with a couple of payments and trading customers; Ethan can share anonymized performance numbers post-call.
[06:43] Ethan: I'll include a small benchmark spreadsheet showing p95/p99 for different model sizes and regions.
[06:48] Jon: Ok let's talk timelines — we're aiming to go to pilot in Jan with production by March. Any blockers?
[06:54] Camila: Sounds doable. The blockers tend to be security review and procurement; we'll align docs and a pilot proposal to fit your procurement cycle.
[07:02] Asha: Procurement will want the SOC 2 and encryption / key management details up front.
[07:06] Camila: Yep, sending those today.
[07:09] [short pause, cross talk]
[07:20] Maya: Something about observability — do you surface per-token cost so we can control spend?
[07:25] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Console includes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. You can set quotas and alerts.
[07:33] Jon: For the Dedicated pool, how does autoscale behave on sudden spikes? We can't afford tail latency during flash growth.
[07:39] Ethan: Autoscale uses predictive warmers and burst capacity; you can configure policy to keep some buffer to avoid cold-starts. For extremely sudden spikes we rely on pre-warmed standby capacity or spillover to hosted if that's acceptable.
[07:53] Maya: Spillover to hosted — is that permitted under compliance for EU-only routes?
[07:58] Ethan: Only if you allow cross-region or cross-jurisdiction spillover. Otherwise we keep the route pinned.
[08:05] Jon: Let's dig into a concrete scenario: region A (EU) goes down. Traffic should fail to region B (US) only for non-PII routes. For payment auth (PII), region must stay EU and we accept degraded throughput. Is that supported?
[08:20] Ethan: Yes, you can mark routes as residency-strict. In that case we'd disable cross-region failover and either throttle or queue requests, or use any standby EU Dedicated replicas you have. You can also configure a degraded-mode model with lower compute to preserve throughput.
[08:36] Asha: For compliance, we'll need an escalation contact and SLA credits spelled out.
[08:41] Camila: We'll include that in the pilot contract appendix.
[08:45] [several minutes of architecture clarifications omitted for brevity but present in notes]
[18:12] Ethan: Quick note on KV cache again — if you rely on session-state we recommend sticky routing within region and a TTL-based replication for critical session keys. That keeps latency low and simplifies failover semantics.
[18:28] Jon: Sticky routing — can that be token-scoped? We have many microservices; need per-route sticky policies.
[18:33] Ethan: Yes, it's configurable per route or per API key.
[18:37] Maya: Any limitations on model variants when failing over? For example, can a fallback be an on-prem private model?
[18:44] Ethan: If you run a Private deployment in your data center we can orchestrate model behavior such that local private models are primary and Hosted/Dedicated are fallback (or vice versa). There are network considerations but it's supported.
[18:57] Asha: For private deployments we need air-gap options and minimal outbound connectivity. Is that offered?
[19:03] Ethan: Yes, our Private package includes an on-prem option with a customer-managed control plane and reduced external dependencies. We'll share the options in the security doc.
[19:12] Maya: Regarding monitoring, do you export traces/tracing headers for distributed tracing?
[19:17] Ethan: We forward trace context and support TraceID propagation; you can correlate per-request with your APM.
[19:23] Jon: Let's confirm the data retention defaults and ability to opt-out of storing full request payloads on Redwood.
[19:29] Ethan: You can choose to disable full payload retention; metadata is still retained for audit. For Dedicated/Private we can meet stricter retention policies.
[19:37] [longer technical back-and-forth about autoscaling knobs and kernel selection omitted for brevity]
[32:05] Camila: Ok, let's circle to action items and next steps. Ethan, you have a perf plan to share?
[32:11] Ethan: Yes I'll draft and include load test scenarios and failover simulations. Need the prompt corpus from Maya.
[32:17] Maya: I'll send a scrubbed prompt set and QPS profile by Tuesday.
[32:22] Camila: I'll email the security pack and pricing. Can we schedule the SE deep-dive the week of 11/23?
[32:29] Jon: That works.
[32:32] Asha: Procurement will also want a sample MSA.
[32:35] Camila: We'll include that.
[32:37] Maya: One last question — how do you measure quality regressions when falling back? We need to ensure the fallback doesn't change decisioning.
[32:45] Ethan: Good point. We do prompt-set based QA; you can register critical prompts and the system will compute similarity metrics, hallucination detectors, and surface regression deltas during rollouts or failover. We can add automated rollback on quality thresholds.
[32:59] Jon: Perfect.
[33:02] Camila: Ok thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts. Anything else from Hypatia?
[33:08] Maya: No, that covers it. Thanks.
[33:11] Jon: Thanks.
[33:12] Asha: Thanks everyone.

Recap (verbatim):

- Schedule SE deep-dive week of 2026-11-23.
